## Features

**Automated Reviews**: Continuous reviews of the pull requests including incremental commits. 

**Summarization**: Generates high-level summary and a technical walkthrough of the PR changes. 

**Line-by-line review**: Provides line-by-line suggestions committable with one click.

**Codebase verification**:  Verifies the impact on the overall codebase and identifies missing changes.

**Insights into your code**:  Ask any questions on your codebase within the pull request 

**Chat about your code** : Chat with the bot around your code. The more you chat, the smarter it gets.

**Issue Validation**:  Validates the PR against the linked issues and identifies other related issues

## Evidence update — the gate is not met: the branch's test target does not compile

### 1. The remote executor cannot produce this evidence (defect filed)

The settling command is `cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh` from `pkgs/id` (the `world_ssh` module is behind the `ssh` feature; without it the new code compiles out, so the earlier 969-green run proved nothing). Two fleet-command runs — [45249821636](https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45249821636) and [45255497015](https://github.com/developing-today/fleet/actions/runs/45255497015) — failed identically **before any test ran**:

```
error: failed to run custom build command for ring v0.17.14
could not execute process …/build-script-build (never executed)
No such file or directory (os error 2)
```

Deterministic, not a flake: the `ring` build-script binary cannot execute in the baked executor image (`aws-lc-sys` is in the same tree). Filed as **dezren39/fleet#111** — any crate with a native build-script dependency of this class is unbuildable in the executor until it is fixed.

### 2. Venue moved to the laptop

Per the remote-builds rule's own fallback (a job that cannot be dispatched successfully falls back, with the reason recorded — this is that record), the suite was run on amd-6 in a fresh worktree of `origin/felix/787-kitty-slice-e-f` (head `00520a8a3`), same command: `cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh` from `pkgs/id`.

### 3. Result: compile failure in this PR's own test code — no tests ran

`error: could not compile id-worlds (lib test) due to 9 previous errors`. All 9 are in the `#[cfg(test)]` code of `crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs`:

- **E0428** (`world_ssh.rs:3269`): `read_until_bytes` is defined twice in the test module — an older 4-argument version at line 3059 (`channel, terminal: &mut vt100::Parser, needle: &str, …`) and a newer 3-argument version at line 3269 (`channel, needle: &[u8], timeout: Duration`).
- **E0061** (`world_ssh.rs:3943`): a test calls `serve_limited(...)` with 5 arguments; the function now takes 6 — the missing argument is this PR's own new `SshServeOptions`.
- **E0308 ×7** (`world_ssh.rs:3328, 3335, 3401, 3403, 3410, 3451, 3495`): test calls written against the newer `read_until_bytes` signature resolve to the older definition and mismatch.

No errors are in `kitty.rs` itself, but the kitty unit tests live in the same lib test target, so **zero tests executed** — the six kitty tests and the `world_ssh::` tests have still never run anywhere: remote runs without `ssh` compiled the module out, and remote runs with `ssh` died at `ring` before reaching this code.

### What is needed

Reconcile the two generations of test helpers in `world_ssh.rs` (one `read_until_bytes`; update the `serve_limited` call with the options argument), then re-run the same command. The full laptop log is on amd-6 at `/home/user/787-kitty-evidence.log`. This PR is **not** merged on this evidence.

**Fix lane update (felix): the test target compiles again; one runtime failure remains, and it is a production trigger defect, not a test defect — not fixed here, diagnosis below.**

## The compile fix — commit `c15154708`

Test code only, in `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs` (+11/−5), no assertions changed:

- The screen-based helper (channel, `&mut vt100::Parser`, `&str` needle; panics on timeout) is renamed `read_until_screen_bytes`, with its four call sites updated (the `read_until` wrapper and the repaint test, whose waits are on rendered screen contents).
- `read_until_bytes` is now only the raw-byte form (channel, `&[u8]` needle, timeout) the kitty tests are written against; its seven call sites resolve to it. The E0428 duplicate and the seven E0308s are gone.
- The `TwoTransports` fixture's `serve_limited` call now passes `SshServeOptions::default()` (the E0061), matching `start_limited`.

## Evidence — laptop (amd-6), worktree at pushed head `c15154708`

The remote executor still cannot build this tree (dezren39/fleet#111), so the run stayed on the laptop, under `fleet-build-lock`:

`cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh` from `pkgs/id` — **1025 passed / 1 failed** (28.16s).

- The six kitty unit tests, all **ok**: `flags_reports_parse_only_the_exact_shape`, `the_filter_consumes_only_the_outstanding_answer`, `verification_flips_active_only_on_the_disambiguate_flag`, `keys_coalesced_with_the_answer_keep_their_order`, `fallback_keeps_held_token_bytes_and_the_owed_pop`, `split_tokens_complete_across_feeds`.
- `world_ssh::` tests: 57 executed, 56 ok. Kitty integration: `kitty_stays_off_without_the_server_opt_in` ok, `kitty_stays_off_when_the_terminal_reports_no_support` ok, `kitty_opt_in_falls_back_when_the_push_does_not_take` ok, `kitty_opt_in_negotiates_verifies_and_frames_split_input` **FAILED**.

## The remaining failure — production activation trigger

`kitty_opt_in_negotiates_verifies_and_frames_split_input` fails deterministically (3/3 isolated re-runs, ~10.1s each) at the "one push + verify burst after detection" assertion: expected 1, got 0. A diagnostic run (assert message patched on the laptop only, since reverted) shows the read buffer is **empty** — after the terminal answers the probe with `CSI ? 0 u`, the server sends nothing at all for the full 10s window. Not a chunking/contiguity issue: the burst is never written until further input arrives.

Root cause, in the raw-mode input path of `world_ssh.rs`: `maybe_begin_kitty()` is invoked only at the top of the inbound-receive routine. That routine's probe-wait loop closes the probe on its 250 ms deadline, and when no held bytes remain it loops into a bare `frames.recv()` park — it does not re-check activation. So once the probe closes with detected support, the push waits until one more input frame arrives and is returned as legacy input, and only the *next* receive call attempts activation. The sibling fallback test passes precisely because it sends another key (`q`), which prods the loop into activating; this test sends nothing after the probe answer, per the design contract that negotiation follows detection.

That is production logic (when activation is attempted), so per lane discipline it is reported, not rewritten here. Suggested shape for the fix, for whoever picks it up: after `close_terminal_probe()` in the probe-wait loop, loop back through the activation check instead of parking on `frames.recv()` — i.e. re-run `maybe_begin_kitty()` before waiting for more input. The test stands as written; it states the design's contract.

Production fix landed — head `0b344c9d2` (on top of `c15154708`). The suite is now fully green with the previously failing test passing.

**The change** — one file, `pkgs/id/crates/id-worlds/src/world_ssh.rs`, `SshIo::recv`, Raw mode (+18 lines, no test touched, no assertion changed): in the probe-wait loop's deadline arm, after `close_terminal_probe()` returns no held bytes, the loop now runs the same activation check the top of `recv()` runs — `maybe_begin_kitty().await`, and if the kitty engine is engaged, returns `kitty_next()` mapped the same way (token / resize / closed) — instead of looping into the bare `frames.recv()` park. When the probe closes without support or without the opt-in, `kitty_may_activate()` is false, the check is a no-op, and the loop parks exactly as before, so the legacy and fallback paths are unchanged. Cancel-safety is preserved: the probe is already taken by `close_terminal_probe()` at that point, and no new await is introduced across the demux.

This matches the diagnosis in the previous comment: the burst (push + verify) was only ever attempted at the top of the *next* `recv()` call, so a terminal that answered the probe and then waited for the push stalled until the user typed again — the extra key in the fallback test was what prodded it into activating.

**Evidence** — laptop (amd-6), worktree reset to the pushed head `0b344c9d2`, under `fleet-build-lock` (the remote executor still cannot build this tree — dezren39/fleet#111): `cargo test -p id-worlds --lib --features ssh` from `pkgs/id`:

- **1026 passed / 0 failed** (27.86s), exit 0. Full log on amd-6 at `/home/user/787-kitty-fix-evidence.log`.
- `world_ssh::tests::kitty_opt_in_negotiates_verifies_and_frames_split_input` — **ok** (previously failing deterministically: expected 1 push+verify burst, got 0).
- Siblings still ok: `kitty_opt_in_falls_back_when_the_push_does_not_take`, `kitty_stays_off_without_the_server_opt_in`, `kitty_stays_off_when_the_terminal_reports_no_support`.
- All six kitty unit tests ok: `flags_reports_parse_only_the_exact_shape`, `the_filter_consumes_only_the_outstanding_answer`, `verification_flips_active_only_on_the_disambiguate_flag`, `keys_coalesced_with_the_answer_keep_their_order`, `fallback_keeps_held_token_bytes_and_the_owed_pop`, `split_tokens_complete_across_feeds`.

No new dependencies. Ready for Felix's merge.
